Lo que ocurre en un escenario no se queda en él.

Encuentra obras, artistas y compañías de teatro, danza, circo e improvisación, y la trayectoria completa de quienes las hacen posibles.

Buscar en Ziater
Buscar

Qué es Ziater

La memoria viva de las artes escénicas.

Ziater es una base de datos abierta de teatro, danza, circo, impro y musical. Cada obra aparece con su elenco, su equipo, sus fechas y dónde verla. Cada artista, con su trayectoria. Consultarla y participar es gratis.

Si eres artista
Tu trayectoria completa en una ficha pública, para compartirla como si fuera tu CV.
Si ya tienes ficha, la reclamas. Si no, la creas en un minuto.
Sube tus obras con elenco, equipo y fotos: tus compañeros quedan enlazados.
Anuncia tus funciones con la sala, la fecha y el enlace a las entradas.
Registra los relevos: elenco original, el actual y quienes han pasado por la obra.
Crear o reclamar mi ficha
Si eres público
Descubre qué hay en cartel, en qué sala y con enlace a las entradas.
Busca cualquier obra, artista, compañía o sala y mira quién hizo qué.
Puntúa lo que has visto y apunta lo que quieres ver.
Sigue a tus artistas favoritos y verás sus obras en tu portada.
¿Falta algo o hay un error? Sugiere el cambio y ayuda a completar las fichas.
Crear mi cuenta gratis

¿Programas una sala o un teatro? Dala de alta y tendrás tu cartelera en Ziater.

What is Ziater

The living memory of the performing arts.

Ziater is an open database of theatre, dance, circus, improv and musicals. Every show appears with its cast, its crew, its dates and where to see it. Every artist, with their career. Browsing and taking part is free.

If you're an artist

Track cast changes: the original cast, the current one and everyone who has been in the show.

Rate what you've seen and save what you want to see.

Synopsis

Vagos y maleantes es un show cómico en el que dos hombres luchan para deconstruir su masculinidad tóxica (y la del público), rompen los tabúes de la sexualidad y definen al nuevo macho ibérico, que ni es tan macho ni tan ibérico. Descúbrelo en el Axel Hotel.

¿Eres un hombre CIS hetero que cree que cocinar es solo para mujeres? ¿Crees que golpear la pared te reafirma como persona? ¿Ni machismo ni Feminismo? Este show te ayudará a deconstruirte. Un espectáculo (LGT(B)) de comedia e improvisación del que saldrás deconstruido.

Battaner y Serna aprovechan su complicidad en el escenario para improvisar con el público y regalaros situaciones únicas, para haceros reír con los sketch de humor y para haceros ver que ser un macho ibérico ya no mola tanto como en los 90's. Estos chicos son los Bertin y Arévalo de nuestra época pero menos machistas, menos nostálgicos y algo más maricas...

Company

La Tetera IMPRO

La Tetera es una productora de espectáculos de teatro de improvisación fundada en 2008 en Granada, actualmente compañía residente en espacios escénicos de Málaga y Granada con representaciones mensuales.

Hemos participado en los eventos de impro mas importantes a nivel nacional, como el Encuentro Nacional de Impro de Zaragoza (ZaragozaImprovisa) o el Festival Internacional de Impro de Baleares (FIIB), además de organizar el Festival de Improvisación de Granada desde 2014 (FESTIG).

Llevamos años investigando sobre la creación instantánea a través de un trabajo colectivo de los componentes de la compañía tanto artística como técnicamente. Creemos en el lenguaje físico y gestual como motor de la improvisación teatral.

Privacy policy

Last updated: 8 November 2026. This is a translation; the Spanish version prevails in case of discrepancy.

At Ziater we take your data seriously: we only collect what we need, we do not sell it and we do not use advertising or third-party trackers. Here we explain which data we process, why, and how you can control it, in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the Spanish Organic Law 3/2018 on Data Protection (LOPDGDD).

1. Who is the controller

The data controller is the owner of Ziater (ziater.com), whose details appear in the legal notice. For any privacy question you can write to us through the contact form.

2. What data we process
Your account data: your email and, if you sign in with Google, the name and photo of your Google account. We never see your password: Firebase Authentication manages it in encrypted form.
Your profile and activity: name, shows you save or have seen, ratings, suggested changes and requests to manage profiles.
Content you publish: pages for shows, artists, companies and venues (texts, dates, credits, links and images), and the change history of those pages.
Artist profiles: professional name, biography, photo, city, roles and career. They may have been created by the person themselves or by others when adding a show.
Contact messages: name, email and the message you send us.
Technical data: the IP address and browser data that reach our servers when you visit the website, and anonymous, aggregated visit statistics (see section 6).
3. Why we use it and on what legal basis
To provide the service (creating your account, saving your lists and ratings, publishing and editing pages): performance of the terms of use you accept when you sign up (art. 6.1.b GDPR).
To maintain a public database of the performing arts, including the professional careers of the people involved: legitimate interest in documenting and spreading culture (art. 6.1.f GDPR). If there is a profile about you, you can claim it, correct it or object to it (section 8).
To answer your messages: your consent when you send them (art. 6.1.a GDPR).
Security, abuse prevention and backups: legitimate interest in protecting the service and the data (art. 6.1.f GDPR).

We do not make automated decisions about you or build profiles for commercial purposes.

4. What is public and what is not

Pages for shows, artists, companies and venues are public, as is each show's average rating and, only if you turn it on, your contributor profile in the ranking. Your email, your individual ratings, your lists, your suggestions and your messages are not public.

5. Who we share data with

We do not sell or transfer your data. To run Ziater we use providers that process it on our behalf (data processors):

Google (Firebase): user accounts and database.
Cloudinary: image storage and optimisation.
Vercel: website hosting and anonymous visit statistics.
GitHub: database backups, in a private repository.

Some of these providers may process data outside the European Economic Area (for example, in the United States). In those cases the transfer relies on appropriate safeguards, such as the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission. We may also disclose data to the authorities when required by law.

6. Statistics and cookies

We do not use advertising or tracking cookies. We count visits anonymously and in aggregate (how many visits each section gets per day), without storing who you are. Statistics that need to store something in your browser are only turned on if you accept them in the cookie notice, and you can change your mind from "Cookie settings" in the footer. The details are in the cookie policy.

7. How long we keep it
Your account data, for as long as you keep the account. If you delete it from "My space" → "Account", your access, email, name and lists are deleted immediately and the rest within 7 days at most.
Public pages and their history, for as long as Ziater exists, because they are part of the cultural database, unless you exercise your right to object or to erasure.
Contact messages, for as long as needed to handle them and one year at most.
Weekly backups, 90 days at most; after that they are deleted.
8. Your rights

You can ask at any time for access to your data, its rectification or erasure, restriction of processing, portability, or object to it, by writing to us through the contact form (reason "Delete my data or exercise another privacy right"). If you have an account, you can also delete it yourself from "My space" → "Account" → "Delete my account and my data". Many things you can do directly from "My space": edit your profile, claim a profile about you or delete your lists.

If you think we have not handled your request properly, you can complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es) or to the data protection authority of your country.

9. Minors

You must be at least 14 years old to create a Ziater account: we ask you when you sign up. If you are a parent or guardian and believe a child under 14 has signed up, write to us through the contact form and we will delete the account.

10. Security

Connections are encrypted (HTTPS), passwords are never stored in plain text and access to data is limited by security rules on the server: each person can only change their own content. Even so, no system is infallible; use a strong, unique password.

11. Changes

If we make important changes to this policy, we will announce them on the website. The date above shows the latest version.

Last updated: 8 November 2026. This is a translation; the Spanish version prevails in case of discrepancy.

Ziater (ziater.com) is an open, free database of the performing arts (the owner's details are in the legal notice). By using the website or creating an account you accept these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use it.

1. The service

Ziater lets you browse and publish information about shows, artists, companies and venues: pages, casts, performance dates, images and ratings. Browsing the website is open and free. To publish, rate or save lists you need an account, which is also free.

2. Your account
You must be at least 14 years old and provide truthful information.
You are responsible for what is done with your account: keep your password safe and do not share it.
You can stop using Ziater whenever you like and ask us to delete your account through the contact form.
3. What you publish
What you publish must be true and respectful. Ziater is a database: correct mistakes, do not make up information.
You may only upload images and texts that are yours or that you have permission to use (for example, your company's poster or photos), crediting the author where appropriate.
You may not impersonate others, publish personal details that are not professional (such as private phone numbers or addresses), or post offensive, discriminatory, illegal content or advertising unrelated to the performing arts.
You remain the owner of your texts and images. By publishing them, you grant us a free, non-exclusive, worldwide licence to display them, adapt them to the website's format (for example, cropping or compressing images) and share them within Ziater and on its social media, for as long as they are published.
Information about shows (titles, dates, casts, venues) is part of the shared database and may remain visible even if you delete your account.
4. Other people's profiles

When adding a show you can include the people who took part in it; this creates a professional profile that the person can claim later. Only include professional, public information. If there is a profile about you, you can claim it to manage it, suggest changes or ask us to correct or remove it (see the privacy policy). Whoever creates a show or a venue manages it; everyone else can suggest changes.

5. Moderation

We may correct, hide or remove content that breaches these terms or the law, and suspend accounts that abuse the service. If you believe something published on Ziater infringes your rights (for example, an image of yours used without permission), let us know through the contact form and we will review it as soon as possible.

6. Links and tickets

Ziater links to third-party websites, such as ticket sellers, venues or social media. We do not sell tickets and we are not responsible for those websites, their prices or changes to or cancellations of performances: always check the details with the venue or the ticket seller.

7. Liability

Much of the content is contributed by users. We work to keep it accurate, but we cannot guarantee that everything is complete or up to date, or that the website is always available. Ziater is provided as is, and we will not be liable for damages arising from the use of the published information, except where the law does not allow this limitation.

8. Ziater's intellectual property

Ziater's name, logo, design and code belong to its owner. You may not copy them or use them to create services that pass themselves off as Ziater.

9. Changes to the terms

We may update these terms. If the change is important, we will announce it on the website. Continuing to use Ziater afterwards means you accept the new version.

10. Governing law

These terms are governed by Spanish law. If you are a consumer, you may also go to the courts of your place of residence and rely on the mandatory consumer protections of your country.

Cookie policy

Last updated: 8 November 2026.

Ziater does not use advertising or tracking cookies, and does not share your browsing with third parties to show you ads. We only store in your browser what the website needs to work, and a few preferences.

What we store in your browser
Session (Firebase Authentication): if you sign in, the browser keeps your session so you are not asked for your password on every visit. It is essential for the service and disappears when you sign out.
Show trailers: we display the video's cover image, downloaded from YouTube (Google) servers without cookies. The player does not load until you click on it; when you do, YouTube may store its own data in your browser. We use its privacy-enhanced mode.
Preferences: light or dark mode, your language, and a flag that shows whether you are signed in so we can show you the right home page.
Your cookie choice: we remember whether you accepted or rejected statistics so we do not ask you again.
Our own visit counter (only if you accept it): a marker with the day's date so the same visitor is not counted twice in the daily statistics. It contains no personal data and is not shared with anyone.
Statistics

If you accept statistics in the cookie notice, we measure visits anonymously and in aggregate with our own counter and with Vercel Web Analytics, which works without cookies and without identifying you. We only see totals (for example, how many people visited show pages on a given day). If you reject them, Vercel Web Analytics does not load and our counter only adds the visit, without storing anything in your browser. You can change your choice at any time from "Cookie settings" in the footer.

How to delete it

You can delete the data stored by Ziater at any time from your browser settings (under "Site data" or "Cookies and site data"). If you do, you will need to sign in again.

More information on how we handle your data in the privacy policy.

Lo que ocurre en un escenario no se queda en él.

Encuentra obras, artistas y compañías de teatro, danza, circo e improvisación, y la trayectoria completa de quienes las hacen posibles.

Buscar en Ziater
Buscar

Qué es Ziater

La memoria viva de las artes escénicas.

Ziater es una base de datos abierta de teatro, danza, circo, impro y musical. Cada obra aparece con su elenco, su equipo, sus fechas y dónde verla. Cada artista, con su trayectoria. Consultarla y participar es gratis.

Si eres artista
Tu trayectoria completa en una ficha pública, para compartirla como si fuera tu CV.
Si ya tienes ficha, la reclamas. Si no, la creas en un minuto.
Sube tus obras con elenco, equipo y fotos: tus compañeros quedan enlazados.
Anuncia tus funciones con la sala, la fecha y el enlace a las entradas.
Registra los relevos: elenco original, el actual y quienes han pasado por la obra.
Crear o reclamar mi ficha
Si eres público
Descubre qué hay en cartel, en qué sala y con enlace a las entradas.
Busca cualquier obra, artista, compañía o sala y mira quién hizo qué.
Puntúa lo que has visto y apunta lo que quieres ver.
Sigue a tus artistas favoritos y verás sus obras en tu portada.
¿Falta algo o hay un error? Sugiere el cambio y ayuda a completar las fichas.
Crear mi cuenta gratis

¿Programas una sala o un teatro? Dala de alta y tendrás tu cartelera en Ziater.

What is Ziater

The living memory of the performing arts.

Ziater is an open database of theatre, dance, circus, improv and musicals. Every show appears with its cast, its crew, its dates and where to see it. Every artist, with their career. Browsing and taking part is free.

If you're an artist
Your whole career on a public profile you can share like a CV.
If you already have a profile, claim it. If not, create one in a minute.
Add your shows with cast, crew and photos: your colleagues get linked.
Announce your performances with the venue, the date and the ticket link.
Track cast changes: the original cast, the current one and everyone who has been in the show.
Create or claim my profile
If you're in the audience
See what's on, where, with a link to tickets.
Search any show, artist, company or venue and see who did what.
Rate what you've seen and save what you want to see.
Follow your favourite artists and see their shows on your home page.
Something missing or wrong? Suggest a change and help complete the pages.

Do you programme a venue or a theatre? Add it and get your listings on Ziater.

Synopsis

Vagos y maleantes es un show cómico en el que dos hombres luchan para deconstruir su masculinidad tóxica (y la del público), rompen los tabúes de la sexualidad y definen al nuevo macho ibérico, que ni es tan macho ni tan ibérico. Descúbrelo en el Axel Hotel.

¿Eres un hombre CIS hetero que cree que cocinar es solo para mujeres? ¿Crees que golpear la pared te reafirma como persona? ¿Ni machismo ni Feminismo? Este show te ayudará a deconstruirte. Un espectáculo (LGT(B)) de comedia e improvisación del que saldrás deconstruido.

Battaner y Serna aprovechan su complicidad en el escenario para improvisar con el público y regalaros situaciones únicas, para haceros reír con los sketch de humor y para haceros ver que ser un macho ibérico ya no mola tanto como en los 90's. Estos chicos son los Bertin y Arévalo de nuestra época pero menos machistas, menos nostálgicos y algo más maricas...
